tool_choice_justification.chosen: Deterministic construction through the official pixelart_workbench (free pixel tools), two official operations: (1) join four copies of the exact seed into the 64x16 sheet (this prepared request), (2) guarded patch_pixels rotating cells 2-4 by 90/180/270 degrees clockwise (next distinct job, not yet prepared).
tool_choice_justification.rejected: animate_image (AI model) with the seed as first_frame data URL.
pixel_art_reasoning: The Working motif is three separated segments orbiting an empty centre in a 16x16 cell at four 100 ms phases; a four-phase orbit of a point-symmetric three-cluster shape is exactly a 90-degree rotation per frame, so the correct in-between frames are lossless pixel permutations of the seed and there is nothing for a generative model to invent.

Retained evidence: the AI animation of this same seed (live.working-animation-01.job, 5 frames returned, frames 1-4 selected) produced an opaque #808080 background in one frame (193 pixels, repaired by guarded patch), then visibly morphing/near-hold segments across phases 2/3 and a jump at the wrap (live.working-animation-repair-01 rejected). The accepted motion live.working-animation-motion-01.candidate is exactly clockwise quarter-turns of the seed executed through official guarded edits.

Local verification: cw rotation dst(x,y)=src(y,15-x) reproduces all four accepted motion-01 cells with 0 visible-pixel differences (counter-clockwise gives 58 differences on cell 1), so the construction policy is pinned to the accepted direction.

Volume and anchor stability, uniform angular velocity and a seamless wrap are guaranteed by construction, which is what the member criteria motion-continuity and transparent-exterior demand; the workbench path also costs no paid generation and carries the actual seed bytes as a data URL (fresh transport, not an old upload handle).
tool_choice_justification.why_join_first: The seed is 16x16 and an edit cannot grow the canvas; join is the official operation that produces the 64x16 destination geometry from the seed bytes. The rotation edit then operates on the official join result id, keeping the whole construction inside official tools.

frame_selection_assembly_policy.summary: Expected step-1 result is already the destination geometry (64x16, cells at x=0,16,32,48), so no frame selection from a larger set is intended. If the provider result differs (gutters, padding, other size or order): retain the raw output, never resize/crop-and-guess or silently drop/duplicate frames; either re-request join with corrected flags or perform a documented lossless cell extraction recording exact source rectangles in play order, each verified pixel-equal to the seed. Step 2 patches 160 pixels (cells 2-4) with expected/replacement pairs computed from the seed; transparent expected value assumed #00000000 (all 224 transparent seed pixels are RGBA 0,0,0,0) and must be confirmed with workbench measure after join (the earlier AI output used #80808000). Play order cell 0->1->2->3->0, each step a further 90-degree clockwise turn at 100 ms.
